analysis: Changes reviewed: (1) docs/reports/README.md only bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one index link at head line 8 to a relative report, 2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md. It is a documentation-only change with no security controls, endpoints, protocol text or threat-model-relevant claims modified. The link target is relative, so it adds no external-resource trust. (2) Added docs/reports/evidence/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup/harness/first_ttft.py is a standalone Python benchmark client. Only the first ~50 of 104 lines were visible in the truncated patch excerpt, and no numbered text unit was supplied for it. The visible part builds synthetic random-word prompts with unique nonces, sends streaming chat/completions requests via urllib to a user-supplied base URL with a Bearer key from the CLI, and times the first token. It does not touch the provider, coordinator WebSocket, App Attest, key custody or cache code, so it does not alter TB-002, TB-011, A-003 or A-015 or T-041. Minor, non-finding observations: the API key is passed as a --key CLI argument, which is visible in the local process list. This is an operator-run dev tool and not a shipped artifact. The prompts are synthetic, so no consumer data (A-001) is involved. Remaining limit: the unseen tail of first_ttft.py (the summary/output portion) was not reviewed. Nothing visible suggests it writes secrets or prompts to disk, but that is unverified. No threat-model updates are needed from this PR.
